approach: Root cause: the reader's "Prompt token headroom" section (reader.rs:641-661) lists each set by component id (frame.verifier, capability.change.verifier), so a reading that edits one prompt file must work out which sets compose it and take the tightest room itself. Seven jobs planned growth past a set's room. Fix it where the figure is given. Add to athena-context/src/lib.rs a pure `prompt_file_path(component_id) -> Option<String>` and `file_headroom(&[HeadroomRow]) -> Vec<FileHeadroom>` that derive file -> composing sets -> smallest `left()` from the same HeadroomRow list the budgets test checks. headroom_section renders one line per file after the existing per-set rows, which stay byte for byte. HeadroomRow, headroom_rows, ReaderInputs and reading.rs are untouched. No prompt file, budget or refusal rule changes. Unlike the previous plan, a new lib.rs test also reads each mapped file from disk and compares it with the compiled-in text, so the path convention is pinned to the real files. Criterion 7's demonstration now names its seam and what fails without the change.

decisions.choice: Derive the per-file table in the brief from the existing HeadroomRow list with a pure function in athena-context; add no field to ReaderInputs and do not touch reading.rs.
decisions.reason: HeadroomRow.components names every component of every set in order (lib.rs:243-244), and `left()` is the room (lib.rs:253). File -> sets -> minimum is therefore a pure function of the rows, so the table cannot drift from the per-set rows or from the budgets test figures (budgets.rs:396-446 builds the same rows with headroom_rows). The only caller of reader_brief is read_once (reading.rs:607) and the rows reach it at reading.rs:629, both unchanged.

rejected.option: Compute the per-file table in athena-core reading.rs and pass it as a new ReaderInputs field
rejected.why: It needs a second field built at reading.rs:629 plus the fixture at briefs.rs:3926, and two views of the same rows could disagree.

rejected.option: A refusal or admission rule that rejects a reading planning growth past a file's room
rejected.why: The reader never saw the per-file figure, so giving it that figure can prevent the failure; the request prefers information over refusal. Expected share of past accepted readings refused: 0%, because none is added.
Budget reader is 1998 of 2000 (docs/system-facts.md), and editing prompt files is out of scope. The brief sits outside the budgeted sets.

decisions.choice: Map a component id to a path by convention: contract and frame.<reader|producer|verifier|planner|critic> to crates/athena-context/prompts/<name>.md, and capability.<id>.<producer|verifier> to crates/athena-cap-<id>/prompts/<role>.md. Any other id (defaults, catalog, an unknown frame or role) returns None and is left out of the table.
decisions.reason: The ids are fixed at lib.rs:34-66 (contract, frame.reader, frame.producer, frame.verifier, frame.planner, frame.critic), and the capability crates use capability.change.* (cap-change lib.rs:19,24) and capability.study.* (cap-study lib.rs:24,29) with include_str!("../prompts/producer.md" / "verifier.md"). defaults and catalog are generated at run time (reading.rs:276-277), so no file can be edited to change them. Returning None for anything unknown means a path is never invented.

rejected.option: Add a path field to PromptAsset
rejected.why: PromptAsset literals appear in many places, including test capabilities (run_pin_tests.rs:43-48 uses the frame consts, and other test capabilities), so the change would spread across crates for no gain.

decisions.choice: Pin the convention with a lib.rs test that, for the contract, each frame and the four real capability sections, reads the mapped path from disk (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../<path>) and asserts the file text equals the compiled-in text.
decisions.reason: The earlier plan's risk was that the convention could be wrong. The existing test at lib.rs:654-666 already reads sibling crates' prompt files and docs/agent-reference.md by relative path, so the pattern exists. A wrong frame name or crate directory fails the test instead of printing a path that does not exist. athena-context already reaches these files by include_str! (lib.rs:655-658).

rejected.option: Test only the string mapping with literal expected paths
rejected.why: It would pass even if a prompt file were renamed or moved, leaving the brief naming a path that does not exist.

decisions.choice: Render the per-file table inside the existing '# Prompt token headroom' section, after the per-set rows, under a plain lead line (no new '#' heading), only when the rows are non-empty.
decisions.reason: The existing per-set lines and the phrase 'costs every set that includes it' are asserted by briefs.rs:4263-4277 and run_pin_tests.rs:1603-1624, so they stay byte for byte. Criterion 2 puts the table under that heading. The no-rows test (briefs.rs:4588-4591) keeps passing.

rejected.option: A separate top-level section in the brief
rejected.why: Criterion 2 asks for the table under '# Prompt token headroom'. A separate section would also need its own empty-rows guard.

files.purpose: Add `FileHeadroom { path, sets, left }`, `prompt_file_path` and `file_headroom` after `headroom_rows`, with unit tests for the shared verifier frame (59 and 36 left), the id -> path mapping, and a disk check that each mapped file exists and equals the compiled-in text.
headroom_section also renders the per-file table (path, composing sets, tightest room) after the unchanged per-set rows, only when the rows are non-empty.
Add the two reader-brief tests: the contract.md line lists every composing set with the minimum room, and no per-file text appears when headroom is empty.
Add a stand-in `change` capability and the test `the_reading_brief_names_the_token_headroom_per_prompt_file`, asserting the per-file lines in the real reading brief.
Add one [Unreleased] / Changed entry naming the root cause, the failure class, the jobs, the fix and the tests; existing entries are not edited.
Append D185 (Case, Decision with root cause, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance); existing entries are not edited.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs, after `headroom_rows`, add `pub struct FileHeadroom { pub path: String, pub sets: Vec<String>, pub left: u64 }` (derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq) with a doc comment: the tightest room among the sets that compose one prompt file; a file listed in several sets costs each of them when it grows. Add `pub fn prompt_file_path(component_id: &str) -> Option<String>`. `contract` returns crates/athena-context/prompts/contract.md. `frame.<role>` with role in reader, producer, verifier, planner or critic returns crates/athena-context/prompts/<role>.md. `capability.<id>.<role>` (split with `strip_prefix("capability.")` and `rsplit_once('.')`) with role producer or verifier returns crates/athena-cap-<id>/prompts/<role>.md. Anything else returns None. Add `pub fn file_headroom(rows: &[HeadroomRow]) -> Vec<FileHeadroom>`: for each row in order and each component id with a path, find the entry by path in a Vec (first-seen order), push the row's set only if not yet listed, and keep the minimum `row.left()`; otherwise push a new entry.

In the lib.rs tests module add three tests, all with `headroom` in the name. `headroom_per_file_takes_the_tightest_of_the_sets_that_compose_it` builds the rows of criterion 3 (verifier (change) 59 left, verifier (study) 36 left), asserts the verifier.md entry lists both sets in row order with left 36, the cap-change verifier.md entry lists only change with 59, and a row listing frame.verifier twice names its set once. `headroom_file_paths_map_every_prompt_component` asserts the mapping cases and None for defaults, catalog, `frame.unknown`, `capability.x.other` and `capability`. `headroom_file_paths_name_the_file_each_component_is_built_from` joins `Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..")` with the mapped path for CONTRACT, the five frames and the four real capability sections, and asserts that `std::fs::read_to_string` equals the compiled-in text (use the include_str! paths already at lib.rs:655-658 for the capability texts).

In crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs `headroom_section`, keep the heading, intro, per-set loop and trailing blank line byte for byte, and insert the per-file block after the loop and before `out.push('\n')`. Call `crate::file_headroom(&inputs.headroom)`. If the result is non-empty, write a lead line `By prompt file (the tightest room across the sets that compose it; plan growth to fit the tightest):` and one line per file: `- {path}: composed by {sets joined by ", "}; tightest room {left} tokens left`. Do not add a new '#' heading.

In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tests add `the_reader_brief_lists_the_tightest_room_per_prompt_file` (three rows composing `contract` with 80, 20 and 41 left; assert the exact contract.md line with all three sets and `tightest room 20 tokens left`) beside briefs.rs:4263, and `the_reader_brief_has_no_per_file_headroom_without_rows` (empty headroom; assert neither the lead line nor `prompts/contract.md: composed by` appears) beside briefs.rs:4588.

In crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs add `struct StandInChange` (id "change"; card, grants, checks, env, admit and pins_repo as PinningStudy, lines 31-77; producer and verifier sections `PromptAsset { id: "capability.change.producer"/"capability.change.verifier", version: 1, text: "stand-in ..." }`) and the test `the_reading_brief_names_the_token_headroom_per_prompt_file`. It captures the reader brief with the Tweak hook as at :1587-1591, does `let mut athena = athena_with(...)`, `athena.capabilities.push(Box::new(StandInChange))`, then `athena.ask("study the demo", &Quiet)`. It asserts the cap-change verifier.md line with the room computed through `athena_context::compose` and `BudgetSet::Verifier.budget()`, and that the context verifier.md line names `verifier (study), verifier (change)` with 0 tokens left (study's frame is composed twice, :1608-1619).

Add one bullet to CHANGELOG.md under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Changed` after the existing bullets (before line 16): the root cause (the reader's headroom section gave per-set rows by component id, not per-file room, so a reading had to find the sets composing a file and take the smallest room itself), the failure class reading-edits-prompt-without-checking-token-budget (20261024-002642-bm4c), job 20261024-002644-1as8 and the other introspected jobs, the fix (`prompt_file_path` and `file_headroom` in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs and the per-file lines in headroom_section), 'no refusal rule (0% of past accepted readings refused)', and the tests (`cargo test -p athena-context headroom`, `cargo test -p athena-context reader_brief`, `cargo test -p athena-core token_headroom`). Append D185 to the end of docs/decisions.md in the D184 format (Case, Decision with the root cause, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance listing what was read, which tests were run and what was not measured, namely whether readers act on the table). Edit no existing entry.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` (fix lints in the new code only). Then run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` to confirm the headroom rows and the docs/system-facts.md budget lines are unchanged. Touch no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, so `--locked` holds.

risks.risk: The path convention is wrong for a future capability crate, or a component id has no file, so the brief shows a wrong path or omits the component.
risks.mitigation: `prompt_file_path` returns None for ids it does not know (defaults, catalog, an unknown frame or role), so a path is never invented. The disk test reads each mapped path for the contract, every frame and the four real capability sections and compares the file with the compiled-in text, so a rename or move fails a test. The per-set rows stay as a fallback.

risks.risk: The stand-in capability in the athena-core test adds a second capability to `athena.capabilities` and could disturb the reader fake or the capability choice.
risks.mitigation: The scripted reader reply fixes `capability: study` (run_pin_tests.rs:170). `Athena::capability` looks up by id (lib.rs:264-270). The stand-in is pushed only in the new test and mirrors PinningStudy's trait methods (run_pin_tests.rs:31-77). The existing test is unchanged.

risks.risk: The brief grows by about one line per prompt file, and a reader could still ignore it.
risks.mitigation: This is not enforced, by design: no refusal rule is added (0% of past accepted readings refused). The table states the tightest room per file in the form the reader needs, and the budgets test remains the backstop after a producer edit. The reader brief has no token budget, and the per-file table only restates figures the section already carries. Whether readers use it is not measured.

risks.risk: The contract file is listed by every set, so its line is long (eight sets in the repository's own rows).
risks.mitigation: Sets are listed once each in row order and the table has at most one line per prompt file, about 15 lines. No other text in the brief changes.

After the loop it calls `crate::file_headroom(&inputs.headroom)` and, when the result is non-empty, writes a lead line and one line per file in the form `- <path>: composed by <set>, <set>; tightest room <n> tokens left`. The existing test `the_reader_brief_shows_the_headroom_of_each_set` still passes, which proves the per-set rows are kept.

demonstrations.method: New unit test `headroom_per_file_takes_the_tightest_of_the_sets_that_compose_it` in the lib.rs tests module. It builds HeadroomRow literals (all fields are pub, lib.rs:240-249) and calls `file_headroom`. The rows are `verifier (change)` with components [contract, frame.verifier, capability.change.verifier], used 1241 and budget 1300 (59 left), and `verifier (study)` with components [contract, frame.verifier, capability.study.verifier], used 1264 and budget 1300 (36 left). It finds the entry for crates/athena-context/prompts/verifier.md and asserts `sets == ["verifier (change)", "verifier (study)"]` and `left == 36`. It also asserts crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/verifier.md lists only `verifier (change)` with 59 left, and that a row that lists frame.verifier twice names its set once.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The shared frame file lists both sets with 36 left; the capability file lists only its own set with 59 left.
demonstrations.fails_without: `file_headroom` does not exist, so the test does not compile. An implementation that took the first row's room (59), summed the rooms (95) or listed one set fails the `36` and both-sets assertions, so the test checks the minimum across composing sets and not one instance.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `athena_context::file_headroom` (added by plan step 1). The fixture is plain HeadroomRow literals, since every field is pub (lib.rs:240-249). Nothing is faked or injected, and the logic under test is not in the fixture. The seam is added by step 1; the HeadroomRow type exists.

demonstrations.method: Two new tests in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, beside the_reader_brief_shows_the_headroom_of_each_set (briefs.rs:4263). `the_reader_brief_lists_the_tightest_room_per_prompt_file` starts from the existing fixture `reader_inputs(&reading())` (briefs.rs:3913, `headroom: vec![]` at :3926) and sets `inputs.headroom` to three HeadroomRow literals that all list `contract` and differ in room: `reader` (80 left), `planner` (20 left) and `verifier (change)` (41 left). It renders `reader_brief(&inputs)` and asserts the brief contains the exact line `- crates/athena-context/prompts/contract.md: composed by reader, planner, verifier (change); tightest room 20 tokens left`. `the_reader_brief_has_no_per_file_headroom_without_rows` leaves `inputs.headroom` empty and asserts the brief contains neither the lead line nor `prompts/contract.md: composed by`. No existing text in the brief contains `prompts/` or the lead line (grep of crates/athena-context/src/briefs found none), so the negative assertion is meaningful.

demonstrations.method: New test `the_reading_brief_names_the_token_headroom_per_prompt_file` in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs, modelled on the test at :1582-1646. athena-core cannot depend on athena-cap-change (cap-change depends on core, per the crate-reach facts), so the test defines `StandInChange`, a capability with id "change" that copies PinningStudy's card, grants, checks, env and admit (run_pin_tests.rs:31-77). The study set composes the frame twice (:1608-1619), so its room is 0 and that file's tightest room is 0.

demonstrations.observes: fmt exits 0. Run the same way, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` exits 0 with no warning in the new code, and `cargo test --locked` passes in full: the new tests of criteria 3, 4 and 5, the existing headroom and reader-brief tests, `the_reader_headroom_rows_equal_the_budget_figures_and_name_shared_files` (budgets.rs:396) and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (the budget lines in docs/system-facts.md are unchanged because no prompt file changes).

With only part of it, `cargo test --locked` fails: no `file_headroom` means athena-context's test target does not compile, and a headroom_section that prints no per-file line fails the contract.md assertion of criterion 4 and the athena-core assertion of criterion 5. Unformatted new code fails `cargo fmt --all --check`. An unused or unlinted item fails clippy under `-D warnings`.
